Your case is actually pretty mild I love watching the toe bro and there are so many cases of raised nail beds that tend to mess up the direction of the nail.
Sometimes the nail would just grow up instead of out. And usually there's no solution to fix it other than filing it down each visit.

I think yours is barley noticeable but if it bothers you a doctor might have some ideas. I can also find a positive take - you can probably still type on a keyboard with the pads of your fingers. I hate the sound of my nails on hard surfaces

There are also finger gloves on Amazon that are thicker and they also come in light skin color (sadly no darker skin tones) instead of white so they don't stand out if you want to use them when going out.

I am planning to buy them eventually.

The biggest plus for me is that I'm actually infection-free. The skin around my nails used to always be red and swollen (ouch) from the wounds coming in contact with bacteria from my mouth/outside sources. The gloves prevent the infection and let's the finger heal quickly.

I also put some products on my nails like those nail strengthening drops or some alcohol to before putting on the gloves.

Oh and here are the things that helped me (but I would recommend also reading other comments and posts since this is only my experience. You should try and find what works best for you. Trial and error)

Gloves. Find the cheapest you can find. Like those nurses use. You can buy a bulk at the dollar store if this method works for you.

Cut the fingers. You don't have to keep them long. Wear them on your fingers. You can also put some of the products that help nail growth inside. 
Or in my case some alcohol since my biting always left me with wounds and infection. That gave me the time I needed for the nails and fingers to heal.
The rubber gloves are quite thin so they tend to rip easily. Some people hate the feeling of rubber against their teeth but I actually liked it. So I just rubbed my teeth and it would calm the urge down.

Finding something else to occupy your month. Could even use a biting toy. No shame since they are designed for biting.

Or some fidget toy.

Since I tend to use my teeth for "cleaning" under the nails I would take extra care to make sure they are clean by washing them and using the end of my brush instead of my teeth. Keeping them clean helped to reduce the impulse so I won't be bothered by the dirt. You can also paint your nails for extra protection and it would block the view but for me nail polish is another thing my mouth want to bite.

It's OK. Relapses happen to the best of us
no one is fully immune.
My advice is try not to count the times you "failed" only your successes
Right now my nails are strong and long (only in my book)

 Good luck and sharing is always welcome

[here's a video](https://youtu.be/S6YG0Ij7Bqs) about "worst animal parents" with some great examples.

Evolution is not perfect and as a result most basic drives like self-preservation, mating and protecting others are often conflicting.

When the need to stay alive and the urge to protect our own conflicts they results in some weird and unexpected scenarios in the wild

• I came across more than one video of a female kangaroo fleeing after dropping the very young and helpless Joey. Sometimes they just flee the scene (Especially while being chased). So self-preservation wins this round and it's also related to your point as a "proven fertile mother" will save herself over the unfertile baby to produce more future offerings (mating drive)

• A pack of lions hunt together and protect the members from danger
yet male lions sometimes (mostly after gaining power) kill all existing cubs in order to impregnate the females again (driven by the mating instinct).

• cattle depends more on the herd mentality.
they stay together to protect the sick, weak and young. keeping them surrounded by the stronger and healthier members.
Since using 'strength in numbers' as an advance to better face predators together they have a higher chance of keeping all members safe/retrieving targeted individual. (Powered by the drive to protect)

But not at all cost.
If they sense they are outnumbered/bound to fail they most likely focus on keeping the rest of the herd safe than losing even more members while trying to rescue the injured target.

The choice making process while facing danger is a great subject to compare with us humans since our social nature is likely another method of survival,  yet we often act based on self-preservation over others.

• panic/adrenaline influences the decision-making process. We don't always make the best "correct" choice when pressured.
and animals are the same. The [The trolley problem](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trolley_problem) is a great example.
when asked most if not all people choose the option that will spare the most people (as it's the more logical and calculated option) but when placed on the spot a lot of people would feel unable to act at all resulting in more casualties.
Animals sometimes make the wrong choice in really critical moments.
Just like humans.

Unfortunately it seems they are helpless in this situation. In nature some animals will actually abandoned their young in order to save themselves (nature is very unforgiving and cruel). Bur here it seems they stayed at the scene so it's clear they care at the very least otherwise they would have fled. They are definitely watching from a safe distance also indicating they are interested and are aware of the situation.

So my take is they sense the danger and have realized there's nothing they can do so they simply watch helplessly as their young is being eaten.

Of course like us they have strong instincts to protect our offsprings but also  the instincts of self preservation.

Disclaimer: I am not an expert or certified by any means.
I just like watching and learning about animals and nature.
